text:
sachin: quick q — when a prefix gets demoted (soft) from node A and later picked up on node B, do we ever need to run a full tombstone sweep before we accept reads? trying to reason about stale prefix entries + demote grace window

lina: short answer: no full sweep. we rely on lease/epoch to prevent visibility holes. but there are edgecases with cold rehydrate where stale tombstones could mask newer writes if lease isn't enforced.

maya: adding detail — demote flow currently does: mark demoted, notify sequencer, evict local residency, and issue demote token with expiry. node B does a handshake to claim prefix and fetch latest meta from sequencer. if handshake succeeds we accept reads.

akeem: where it breaks is if node A demoted but still had in-flight writes that didn't make it to sequencer before eviction. node B's fetch sees older seqno and thinks it's up-to-date.

ops: we saw this in prod once — short read-after-write failure during a manual rebalance. We fixed by extending demote token hold by 200ms which reduced repros but not a real fix.

lina: proposal: augment handshake with a short gap-check RPC: after node B fetches meta, it asks node A (if still reachable) for any pending tail writes for this prefix. if none or A unreachable, fallback to sequencer tail.

maya: pseudo: ```
// node B
meta = sequencer.fetch(prefix)
tail = probeOwner(prefix)
if tail > meta.seqno:
  apply tail
else
  proceed
```

sachin: probeOwner sounds ok but adds latency to takeover path. can we make it async and serve reads under a safe token?

lina: yes — two-phase: 1) claim with provisional lease allowing reads but marking them as possibly stale (metrics flagged), 2) in parallel probeOwner and reconcile if needed; if reconciliation finds newer writes, either patch by streaming delta or escalate to reject short window reads and emit rollback markers.

akeem: concern: streaming delta requires we store per-prefix tail deltas for small period or have owner replay from WAL. both are doable but storage/complexity increases.

ops: another option: extend prefix demote to publish a short-lived 'inflight-window' watermark. any new demote must wait until inflight-window is drained. that reduces frequency of needing cross-node probes. but it hurts eviction throughput under heavy churn.

maya: tradeoffs table (short):
- probeOwner: low steady-state cost, extra RTT on takeover, simpler correctness
- inflight-window: simpler takeover, higher eviction latency
- provisional-lease+reconcile: middle ground, complexity on reconcile path

sachin: I lean to provisional-lease+async probe. users care more about correctness than few 100ms takeover latencies, but we should expose metric and flag apps that see provisional reads.

lina: implementation notes: tag reads with header `x-prefix-provisional: true|false` and add a dashboard for provisional read rate + reconcile corrections. also add a small counter for 'reconciled-records' per-prefix.

akeem: one operational failure mode: owner crashes mid-probe and never replies. need timeout and fallback to sequencer-only reconciliation. also ensure probes are rate-limited to avoid thundering herd on busy prefixes.

ops: I'll add a K8s chaos test to simulate owner crash during takeover and a load test with 10k prefixes churn.

maya: will draft a small RFC with APIs: `ClaimPrefix(provisional bool)` and `ProbeOwner(prefix) -> tailSeq, lastWriteTS`. Also include migration plan and metric names.

sachin: thanks — please ping infra for perf numbers. Also add example log line we can search: `prefix_takeover provisional=true prefix=... reconciled=42` :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Note: Created issue INF-8238 for RFC and test plan (link: https://redwood.example/INF-8238)

lina: cool. one more note — ensure replication/replica followers honor provisional tags (don't compact away deltas too early).

akeem: ack. I'll draft the reconcile streaming API shape and run it by you all tomorrow.

sachin: perfect. moving to RFC stage. thanks everyone :)
